title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: An ADNOC Logistics vessel was hit in UAE waters on Tuesday and another tanker was struck off Oman, so the sea war is not over even as Brent dipped below $90. Online demand is at its peak with the Amazon and noon 11.11 sales, while Saudi air links stay patchy.

gauges.label: Brent intraday low, Tuesday
gauges.note: First time below $90 since 31 August; about 23% under the 30 October peak near $118 (Gulf News, 11 Nov)

gauges.label: Ships anchored off Fujairah and Khor Fakkan
gauges.note: As of 8 November; Hormuz transits in single digits to low double digits a day vs about 138 in 2025 (gCaptain, 10 Nov)

gauges.label: Ships attacked in the region in October
gauges.note: Highest monthly total of the war (Washington Institute data via Reuters, 10 Nov)

gauges.label: Emirates SkyCargo revenue, April–September
gauges.note: On 1% less tonnage (1.24m tonnes); network at 91% of pre-disruption (STAT Times, 5 Nov)

gauges.label: Global air cargo spot rate, week 43
gauges.note: Still the latest; up 38% on the year (WorldACD via STAT Times, 2 Nov)

stories.headline: ADNOC Logistics vessel hit in UAE waters; another tanker struck off Oman
body: ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in the Gulf on Tuesday afternoon. It gave no details on the ship, the damage or the crew. Separately, UKMTO said a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile about 19 nm northeast of Lima, Oman, at 1338 UTC on Tuesday; the crew are safe.

The JMIC keeps the Hormuz threat at SEVERE. Daily transits are in single digits to low double digits, against about 138 a day in 2025. About 162 ships were at anchor near Fujairah and Khor Fakkan on 8 November.
stories.soWhat: New: an attack inside UAE waters on a UAE-owned fleet. War-risk cover and east-coast congestion stay; do not cut sea surcharges because oil fell.

stories.headline: Iran says it hit three tankers on 'unauthorised routes'
body: Iranian state media said the IRGC Navy hit three tankers on Sunday for using "unauthorised routes", and that two caught fire after hitting mines. A tanker managed by Navig8, majority owned by ADNOC Logistics & Services, was on fire off Oman.
The IMO counts 130 incidents in the region since late February, with at least 25 seafarers killed. Oil has reached Oman's shore and satellite images show spills off Oman and the UAE.
stories.soWhat: Iran is policing which routes ships use. Expect carriers to keep Gulf calls thin and blank sailings likely; keep customers on east-coast and road options.

stories.headline: Saudi air: flydubai off Riyadh to 16 November, Emirates may not return until late November
body: flydubai has cancelled Riyadh and Abha flights through 16 November and shows them bookable from 17 November. Dammam was bookable from 10 November. Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam flights stay cancelled through 19 November.

Emirates' system showed its Riyadh and Dammam flights cancelled on 8–13 November, with none returned for 17 or 21 November; EK815 and EK821 show as scheduled on 28 November. Saudi Arabia said an attempted attack hit an Aramco building in Riyadh after Houthi missile claims on 8 November.
stories.soWhat: New: Emirates' Riyadh return now looks like late November. Riyadh express needs a road plan for at least two more weeks.

stories.headline: Brent breaks below $90 for the first time since August
body: Brent settled at $92.57 on Monday and fell below $90 on Tuesday, touching $89.65, about 23% under its 30 October peak near $118. It was at $91.98 early on Wednesday. Both benchmarks are down about 20% this month.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told G7 ministers that sanctions and the blockade are working, so major combat is not needed. The US blockade of Hormuz stays for now, and LNG traffic through the strait is at its highest since the war began.
stories.soWhat: New: below $90. Fuel relief is now real for road and air costs; set the December fuel surcharge rule this week before customers ask.

competitors.name: Amazon.ae and noon
competitors.headline: 11.11 sales run to 12–13 November, sold on 15-minute to 2-hour delivery
body: Amazon.ae's 11.11 sale runs 5–12 November. Prime members get free Amazon Now delivery above Dh25 and free Rush 2-hour delivery above Dh100. noon's sale runs 5–13 November with up to 90% off, daily Dh11, Dh111 and Dh1,111 flash deals, and noon Minutes 15-minute delivery.
competitors.soWhat: Peak volume lands this week and next, and both platforms push their own fast fleets. Offer sellers outside those fleets our returns and next-day capacity now.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Cargo revenue up 52% in the half on 1% less tonnage
body: Emirates SkyCargo carried 1.24 million tonnes from April to September, down 1%, but cargo revenue rose 52%. It took five new Boeing 777 freighters and added Almaty and Zhengzhou. Emirates Group profit before tax fell 66% to AED 4.1 billion on fuel costs. dnata is opening a new AED 100 million logistics facility in Dubai South.
competitors.soWhat: The carrier is earning on yield, not volume. Do not expect cheaper Dubai uplift soon; lock block space for peak and pass through air rates.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Launches Aramex Data Center Logistics in the GCC, Asia and the US
body: Aramex launched a service for AI data centre builds, starting in the GCC, Southeast Asia and Taiwan, and the US South, with Abu Dhabi and Riyadh named. It covers heavy construction kit, AI racks by charter or secure road, white-glove placement and spare parts. Group CEO Amadou Diallo: "A data center is only as fast as its slowest delivery."
competitors.soWhat: A new high-value product line. Sales needs a target list of UAE and Saudi data centre builders and a pricing model for project work.

opportunities.title: 11.11 overflow and returns
opportunities.text: Sales end 12–13 November. Sellers outside the Amazon and noon fleets need peak and returns capacity this week.

opportunities.title: UAE–Riyadh road express
opportunities.text: flydubai is off Riyadh to 16 November, Etihad to 19 November and Emirates may not return before 28 November.

opportunities.title: East-coast congestion services
opportunities.text: About 162 ships wait off Fujairah and Khor Fakkan. Offer drayage, storage and trucking into Dubai for cargo that lands there.

opportunities.title: Data centre project logistics
opportunities.text: Our new service names Abu Dhabi and Riyadh. Turn it into a pipeline of build projects.

watchouts.title: Attacks inside UAE waters
watchouts.text: An ADNOC Logistics vessel was hit on Tuesday. Insurers may reprice UAE-side calls.

watchouts.title: Fuel surcharge pressure
watchouts.text: Brent touched $89.65. Customers will push for fast cuts; oil can jump back on one headline.

watchouts.title: Air rates stay high
watchouts.text: SkyCargo revenue is up 52% on flat tonnage. Our air buy cost is unlikely to fall soon.

watchouts.title: Riyadh security
watchouts.text: An attempted attack hit an Aramco building in Riyadh. Saudi air schedules can slip again.

moves.title: Decide the December fuel surcharge rule
moves.text: Brent is below $90. Set the level and number of days that trigger a cut, and tell key accounts first.

moves.title: Hold sea war-risk charges
moves.text: A UAE-owned vessel was hit in UAE waters. Keep Gulf sea surcharges and explain why with today's facts.

moves.title: Sell 11.11 overflow and returns
moves.text: Call mid-size UAE sellers today with next-day and returns pickup through 20 November.

moves.title: Extend Riyadh road cover to end-November
moves.text: Emirates may not fly Riyadh until 28 November. Book trucks and tell express customers the transit time.

moves.title: Lock Dubai air block space for peak
moves.text: SkyCargo is pricing for yield. Secure allocations now rather than waiting for spot rates to ease.

moves.title: Build a data centre target list
moves.text: List UAE and Saudi data centre projects and draft a project-pricing template for the new service.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
